text:
**The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a strong choice if you want one station for either appliance. It has a **2,600 W inverter**—enough headroom for a typical single-burner induction cooktop rated up to 1,800 W—and a **2,073.6 Wh battery**. ([Product details and recommendation](https://dealectric.com/power-station-that-can-run-an-induction-cooktop))

For a kettle, check its wattage label and make sure it’s below the station’s 2,600 W output. The battery size determines how long you can cook or how many times you can boil water; a litre of water takes roughly **90–110 Wh** to boil, before losses. ([Power requirements and boil estimate](https://homepowerfacts.com/can-it-run/induction-cooktop/))
